course_identity.title: Fundamentals of Computing and Artificial Intelligence

syllabus.course_description: A pre-university academic course introducing foundational structures of computing and artificial intelligence. Students develop computational reasoning, examine how intelligent systems represent information, reason, learn from data, and make decisions, and investigate how such systems should be evaluated and used responsibly through guided conceptual and computational practice.
learning_outcomes: Explain how computational problems can be represented and approached through algorithms, abstractions, and structured reasoning.
Explain foundational ideas through which intelligent systems represent information, reason, and make decisions.
Describe how machine learning systems learn patterns from data and distinguish learning from rule-based computation.
Conduct guided computational investigations and interpret observable system behavior using appropriate evidence.
Analyze basic relationships among data, models, predictions, evaluation, and intelligent-system behavior.
Evaluate selected limitations, reliability concerns, human implications, and responsible-use considerations of artificial intelligence.
learning_progression: Evaluation, human interaction, and guided inquiry

modules.module_intent: Establish the computational reasoning foundation required for later study of artificial intelligence.
learning_activities: Trace and compare simple algorithms.
Express a bounded problem through structured computational steps.
Use small Python-based experiments to connect abstract reasoning with observable computation.

modules.module_intent: Introduce artificial intelligence as the construction of systems that represent information and perform structured reasoning under different conditions.
learning_activities: Model a small search or decision problem.
Compare alternative representations of the same information.
Reason through a simple decision where available information is incomplete.

modules.module_intent: Develop a foundational understanding of how computational systems learn patterns from data and how learned behavior can be evaluated.

source_stems.stem: Mathematical and Statistical Foundations of Learning

learning_activities: Inspect and describe a small dataset.
Run a guided learning experiment using a simple model.
Compare predictions with observed outcomes.
Investigate how changes in data can affect model behavior.

modules.module_title: How Intelligent Systems Perceive and Communicate
modules.module_intent: Connect foundational learning concepts to systems that process visual and language information without turning specialized AI domains into separate survey courses.
learning_activities: Compare how text and images can be represented computationally.
Observe the behavior of simple recognition or language systems.
Trace information through a simplified intelligent-system architecture.

modules.module_title: Decision Making, Adaptation, and Autonomous Behavior
modules.module_intent: Show how representation, reasoning, and learning combine to support decisions and adaptive behavior in intelligent systems.
learning_activities: Analyze a bounded decision-making scenario.
Compare fixed rules with adaptive behavior.
Model a simple agent interacting with an environment.

modules.module_title: Evaluating Intelligent Systems and Conducting Guided Inquiry
modules.module_intent: Integrate the course through evidence-based evaluation of intelligent-system behavior, limitations, human implications, and responsible use.

source_stems.stem: AI Evaluation, Safety, Ethics, and Societal Impact

learning_activities: Formulate a bounded question about an intelligent system.
Design and conduct a guided computational investigation.
Collect and interpret observable evidence.
Discuss limitations and responsible-use implications.
Communicate findings through a concise academic artifact.

assessment.approach: Evidence-based and developmental assessment through conceptual reasoning, guided computational investigation, and academic communication rather than high-stakes examination.

major_evidence.evidence: Selected explanations, models, comparisons, and reasoning artifacts demonstrating progression across foundational concepts.
Small guided experiments in which the student observes, analyzes, and explains computational or intelligent-system behavior.
A bounded investigation connecting a research question, computational evidence, interpretation, limitations, and responsible-use considerations.

alignment: Concept and Reasoning Portfolio supports foundational conceptual and computational reasoning outcomes.
Computational Investigations support experimentation, model-behavior analysis, and evidence interpretation outcomes.
Guided Final Inquiry integrates intelligent-system understanding, evaluation, research reasoning, and academic communication.

upon_completion: Engage with deeper study of machine learning, intelligent systems, or computational methods.
Undertake more independent computational experiments with appropriate scaffolding.
Formulate bounded research or project questions involving computing and artificial intelligence.
Progress toward RXI research- and project-based study at greater learning depth.
